# PostureCheckOS

PostureCheckOS is a Ziti posture check that a device passes if it runs one of the listed operating systems in one of the listed versions.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | posture check of type `OS`, `/edge/management/v1/posture-checks` |
| Updated with | `PATCH`: a setting that is left out of the spec is left alone in Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/posturecheck/os.yaml`](../../examples/posturecheck/os.yaml):

```yaml
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: PostureCheckOS
metadata:
  name: supported-os
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: supported-os
    operatingSystems:
      - type: Linux
        versions:
          - ">=5.0.0"
      - type: macOS
        versions:
          - ">=13.0.0"
    roleAttributes:
      - managed-devices
```

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the posture check. |
| `operatingSystems` | list of objects, required |  | `operatingSystems` | OperatingSystems that pass the check. Ziti keeps one entry per type, so each type may be listed once, and their order does not matter. |
| `operatingSystems[].type` | string, required |  | `operatingSystems[].type` | Type of operating system. One of `Windows`, `WindowsServer`, `Android`, `iOS`, `Linux`, `macOS`. |
| `operatingSystems[].versions` | list of strings |  | `operatingSystems[].versions` | Versions constraint (e.g., [">=10.0.0"]). Ziti keeps them as a set, so their order and duplicates do not matter. |
| `roleAttributes` | list of strings |  | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes service policies select the posture check by, as "#attribute". |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

The provider also sends `typeId: OS`.

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

## How it behaves

- Ziti keeps one entry per operating system type, in the order of the types, and the versions of an entry as a set. The spec may list them in any order; the API server rejects a type that is listed twice.
- A posture check does nothing on its own: name it in `postureCheckRoles` of a [`ServicePolicy`](servicepolicy.md), as `@name` or by a role attribute.

## When something goes wrong

- Ziti answers `400` about a version: versions are semantic version constraints such as `>=13.0.0`.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
